en.title: Justice Laws: language marks in the wrong form in 11 historical notes
en.summary: English historical notes mark language-specific amendments (E) and (F); French notes use (A) and (F). In 11 places of the consolidation the mark has the form of the other language: English note of the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, s. 49: “223(A)”; French notes with “(E)” in the Criminal Code, s. 183; Olympic and Paralympic Marks Act, ss. 3, 4 and 8; Canada Labour Code, s. 47.1; Family Orders and Agreements Enforcement Assistance Act, s. 49; Royal Canadian Mounted Police Superannuation Regulations, ss. 57 and 59; Natural Health Products Regulations, ss. 28 and 32.
en.impact: The marks remain readable; they are harder to read by machine and to search. No effect on the law.
en.correction: The Department of Justice decides how to correct each place in the consolidation or the XML; the evidence gives the wording of each language version.

fr.title: Lois du Canada : marques de langue sous une forme erronée dans 11 notes historiques
fr.summary: Les notes anglaises emploient (E) et (F); les notes françaises, (A) et (F). À 11 endroits de la codification, la marque a la forme de l’autre langue, par exemple Code criminel, art. 183, note française : « ch. 20, art. 366(E) »; Loi sur le recyclage des produits de la criminalité et le financement des activités terroristes, art. 49, note anglaise : « 223(A) ».
